acceptance.criterion: resume (the plugin's own `session-watchdog-resume` action) clears the hold AND re-arms the still-claimed attempts so the held work continues through the EXISTING parked-attempt machinery — proven by observing dispatch after resume
acceptance.evidence: raw/driver.result.json checks D1/D4/D5/D6/D7. The hold and the resume are driven through the REAL watchdog plugin (its built dist mounted on the same stub ctx): D1 `session-watchdog-hold` writes the durable file; D4 `session-watchdog-resume` returns resumed:true and the file is gone; D5 the next kick through the SAME `installTeamScheduler` machinery delivers (1 delivery); D6 the delivered task carries a live attempt of its own; D7 the still-claimed case: attempt 2 frozen while held, then re-armed to attempt 3 with a fresh attemptId by the existing `beginTaskAttempt`/park path — the adopted machinery's own generation semantics, NOT a cancel/recreate. Nothing in the resume path calls `agent_teams_resume` or `haltTeamWork`.

acceptance.criterion: the tool boundary refuses `agent_teams_claim_task`/`agent_teams_update_task` for a held team with a LOUD, named reason (the claim path has no halted guard today — measured), while leaving the team's records byte-untouched
acceptance.evidence: checks E1/E2/E3/E4. Both tools are driven through the REAL registered definitions (`apply` from lib/index.js). E1 claim_task: throws `team pause-probe is held by the team watchdog (hold 1b752647-… since …: silence); the team must be released with the watchdog's own session-watchdog-resume action before any further work`. E2 update_task throws the same named refusal. No re-arm is claimed for an attempt that the parked-attempt map considers CURRENTLY parked with the same id (`scheduler.js:515-518` deliberately does not re-dispatch it — that is upstream's 'a resident idle member may keep an attempt open' policy). D7 measures the recovery branch that DOES re-arm (a fresh scheduler install = a cold process), which is the branch the design's §3.2 names.
